notes:
The repository is not a device. It is a Zephyr RTOS integration module for micro-ROS plus a sample application, not a concrete instrument, robot, sensor or actuator. README.md:4 ('# micro-ROS module for Zephyr') and package.xml:6 ('micro-ROS tools for Zephyr RTOS') describe the deliverable; README.md:10 says it needs colcon 'in order to build micro-ROS packages'; CMakeLists.txt:5-10 adds modules/libmicroros to ZEPHYR_EXTRA_MODULES and builds project(microros_sample_app) from src/main.c. modules/libmicroros/CMakeLists.txt:35-55 builds and links the micro-ROS static library, and :76-94 builds only a serial, serial-USB or UDP transport library. modules/libmicroros/Kconfig:1-7 exposes 'micro-ROS Support'; :16-29 selects a transport; :80-110 sets middleware capacities (nodes, publishers, subscribers, clients, servers, history, MTU), not device capabilities or limits. The transport sources are byte pipes only: modules/libmicroros/microros_transports/udp/microros_transports.c:24-103 and modules/libmicroros/microros_transports/serial/microros_transports.c:53-104 open, read and write a socket or UART; neither exposes a device command or state.

The only executable application in the pinned tree is the demo: src/main.c:60-68 creates node 'zephyr_int32_publisher' and publisher 'zephyr_int32_publisher' of std_msgs/msg/Int32; src/main.c:70-77 runs a 1000 ms timer; src/main.c:33-40 publishes the current msg.data and increments it; src/main.c:84-89 spins forever. That is a heartbeat/demo counter with no physical unit, no measured quantity, no command, no stop path and no reset; it is not a device interface. README.md:18 gives the board only as an example ('For example for disco_l475_iot1 board'), and README.md:44-49 states the software 'has neither been developed nor tested for a specific use case' and warns to adjust it before any safety-relevant use. The card itself has empty entry_symbols (task.json:27) and models (task.json:28), and MHS/registry/repos/robots/micro-ros__micro_ros_zephyr_module.json:38 records 'NO_ENTRY_SYMBOL: no AST device class or env registration found'.

The tree contains no .msg, .srv, .action, .launch, Python, URDF or xacro file; git ls-tree at 229ffc0e131ee7942db3bb2e731fb8851583bb25 lists build/configuration files, CI metadata, transports, the sample and documentation. The only ROS message is the standard Int32 used by the demo. A RosDriver for this heartbeat topic would have to invent a device, a capability and an output meaning, and would not preserve a genuine primary control or step interface. There is no concrete device model, unit range, motion interface or safety bound to source. The card's family:ros/RosDriver label comes from the static scan and does not make the module a device. No package code was written, no gate was run, no hardware was attached, the clone is unchanged, and task.json is unchanged. This is a proposed skip for registry override review.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Accepted the skip proposal NOT_A_DEVICE after reading the cited lines: the repository is the micro-ROS module for Zephyr RTOS (README.md:4, package.xml:6) that builds the micro-ROS static library and a serial, serial-USB or UDP transport (modules/libmicroros/CMakeLists.txt), and its only application is a demo node that publishes an incrementing std_msgs/Int32 on zephyr_int32_publisher once a second (src/main.c:33-40, 60-77); the tree has no Python, .msg, .srv, .action or launch file and no device model, unit, command or stop. The registry already routes the sibling gh.micro-ros/micro_ros_arduino as bridge-runtime/transport, so the override proposal uses the same shape (a skip/not-device entry would serve equally). The author wrote no package code; the only file the review added is the check-report.json of the gate run (G1, G2, G3 and G9 fail because there is no package; stable digest sha256:962879f9f425fb8d1efc2a92f047ccb9b099886bad35c0202bff450e7324b786).
